newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sumitomo Bank says FDIC not probing U.S. unit.
newsitem.headline: Sumitomo Bank says FDIC not probing U.S. unit.

text.p: Sumitomo Bank Ltd said on Tuesday that the U.S. Federal Deposit Insurance Corp (FDIC) had not launched an investigation of one of its U.S. units.

Sumitomo said in a statement that it had been informed by a subsidiary, Sumitomo Bank of California, that two employees of the unit had filed an appeal with the FDIC claiming that the unit's loan policies ran afoul of U.S. regulations.

"It is not true that the FDIC has launched a probe of the American unit over the issue, and the unit has been managed under U.S. regulations. Therefore, we believe, as Sumitomo Bank of California said earlier, that (the allegation) was groundless," Sumitomo said in the statement.

Earlier, Kyodo News Agency reported that two loan examiners filed suit against the Sumitomo unit in California for compensation for losses they say they suffered after refusing to go along with the bank's senior managers in extending loans.
Kyodo said the plaintiffs issued a statement saying they had already asked the FDIC to investigate the bank's loan policies.
Sumitomo Bank of California issued a statement in San Francisco on Monday accusing the two employees of carrying out a negative media campaign against the bank. It said their claims were groundless.
Sumitomo Bank's shares tumbled in late Tuesday afternoon trade after media reports about the U.S. subsidiary.
The shares closed down 80 yen at 1,770 on turnover of about five million shares, making Sumitomo Bank the seventh-most heavily traded issue on the first section of the Tokyo bourse.
